heroHeadline: Day 82 — Wana Tribal Chief Killed in IED Blast; Bajaur Polio Police Shot; Taliban Enacts Child Marriage Law
heroSubtitle: On May 18, 2026 (Day 82 of Operation Ghazab lil-Haq), TTP-linked violence continues on two fronts: an IED blast in Wana Bazaar, South Waziristan, killed Ahmadzai Wazir tribal chief Malik Tariq Wazir and two others, targeting a key jirga mediator known for peace advocacy; and two police constables (Syed Aziz and Qadir) were shot dead by motorcycle gunmen while guarding anti-polio vaccination teams in Bajaur's Salarzai area on the first day of Pakistan's nationwide polio campaign. The Taliban also enacted a new 31-chapter family law titled 'Principles of Separation Between Spouses,' approved by Supreme Leader Hibatullah Akhundzada, codifying child marriage and treating silence of unmarried girls as marriage consent — drawing immediate international condemnation. Pakistan's 'decisive action' consensus against TTP sanctuaries in Afghanistan continues with no new confirmed cross-border strikes since May 5 (Dangam, Kunar). Three journalists — TOLO News presenters Mansoor Niazi (Day 12 in custody) and Imran Danish (Day 10), and Paigard News Agency head Jawid Niazi (Day 13) — remain in Taliban detention with Taliban prosecutors planning trial proceedings. The Urumqi non-escalation framework remains under severe stress from five TTP mass-casualty attacks of May 9–14 that killed 30+ Pakistani security forces. No formal ceasefire and no Urumqi Round 2 date have been announced; China remains silent since April 8.
footerNote: Data sourced from UNAMA, SIGAR, ACLED, Brown University Costs of War Project, US DoD, Reuters, BBC, Al Jazeera, Tolo News, Dawn, Geo News, HRW, OHCHR, OCHA
